title: The Price of Pride
summary: A boastful wrestler claims he can lift anything in the empire. Birbal challenges him to lift a single grain of sand under impossible conditions.
full_text:
A colossal wrestler from the Punjab named Rustam-e-Hind arrived at Emperor Akbar's court. He was seven feet tall, with arms like tree trunks and a chest like an iron anvil. He had defeated every champion in the northern provinces and was swollen with insufferable pride.

Standing in the center of the Diwan-i-Am, the wrestler flexed his muscles and roared: 'Emperor Akbar! There is no weight on earth I cannot lift! I can lift two war elephants upon my shoulders! I challenge your courtiers: name any physical object in your empire, and if I cannot lift it above my head, I shall forfeit five thousand gold coins!'

The courtiers looked at the giant in awe, convinced that no human could defeat his challenge.

Birbal stepped forward with a gentle smile: 'Pahalwanji, your strength is truly magnificent. But do you swear that you can lift any physical object in this kingdom?'

'I swear by my ancestors!' the wrestler bellowed. 'Name your rock, your pillar, your cannon!'

Birbal walked into the palace garden, picked up a single, tiny grain of dry river sand between his thumb and forefinger, and placed it upon the marble floor in front of the wrestler.

The wrestler laughed mockingly: 'A grain of sand? Is this a joke? I can lift a mountain, and you ask me to lift a grain of sand?'

'Yes,' Birbal said calmly. 'You must lift this single grain of sand above your head. However, you must adhere to three strict conditions:

'First, you must not use your hands, your feet, your mouth, your toes, or any part of your body.

'Second, you must not use any stick, spoon, blower, magnet, cloth, or physical tool.

'And third, you must lift it using only the colossal strength of your proud voice and your boastful arrogance!'

The wrestler stood frozen, his face turning bright scarlet. 'How can any man lift a physical object without touching it or using a tool? That is impossible!'

Birbal's voice rang clear across the hall:

'Precisely, Pahalwanji! If all your towering pride, your booming voice, and your magnificent arrogance cannot move even the smallest speck of dust without the humble labor of physical touch, why do you strut across the earth as if you were a god? True strength does not brag; it serves.'

The giant wrestler hung his head in profound shame, forfeited his gold coins to the poor, and bowed to Birbal, cured forever of his foolish vanity.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Price of Pride"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
